QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_34

question.text: Yield to Maturity (YTM) of a bond is defined as:

answer.text: The discount rate that equates the present value of all future cash flows from the bond with its current market price
The annual coupon payment divided by the face value of the bond
The total dividends paid by the bond issuer over the life of the bond
The difference between the face value and the issue price of the bond

explanation.text: The Logic: YTM is the rate that equates the present value of all future cash flows from a bond with the current price of the bond. It is the discount rate implied in the bond's value at a point in time. The Trap: Coupon divided by face value (option B) is the coupon rate, not YTM. Dividends (option C) apply to equity, not bonds. Face value minus issue price (option D) is not the definition of YTM. Note: Because YTM depends on the current bond price, it changes as the price changes; it is not the same as the bond's stated coupon rate.
